clue.text: Build these right in the town centre

definitions.text: Build these right in the town centre

parts.words: Build these right in the town centre
parts.note: the main shopping thoroughfare of a British town sits in its centre, so the clue reads as a planning instruction for where to put the principal street

explanation.surface: A planner insists the new buildings go right in the middle of town.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the HIGH STREET is the main shopping street of a town, so 'these' are what belongs in the town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal shopping street of a British town runs through its centre, which is where the clue tells you to put it.

clue.text: Pop's wine

definitions.meaning: to pop something is to pawn it
a German white from the Rhine

explanation.definitionFit: To pawn something is to put it in pawn, slang verb sense; it is also a Rhenish white wine.

clue.text: Song of joy

explanation.definitionFit: A part-song for several unaccompanied voices is one sense; delight or merriment is the other.

clue.text: Alone; like Nelson

definitions.meaning: Admiral Nelson lost his right arm in battle, so had only one

explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unaided is one sense; Admiral Nelson, who lost an arm, literally had only one hand.

clue.text: You need legs for this race!

definitions.text: You need legs for this race!

parts.words: You need legs for this race!
parts.note: seems to say running needs legs; in fact this race is split into stages called legs, run by team members in turn

explanation.surface: An obvious remark that running requires legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A team running event is divided into stages called legs, each run by a different member passing a baton.

clue.text: Disentangle, ie, extract

indicators.note: untangling the letters of 'ie' and 'extract' sorts them into a new order

explanation.surface: A gloss explaining what it means to disentangle: that is, to pull out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and 'Disentangle' also shuffles IE and EXTRACT.
explanation.definitionFit: To free something from a tangle or difficulty is to release it, pulling it clear.

clue.text: National tax

definitions.meaning: a person of a particular nation, here one from Scotland
an old local levy or payment, as in going free of payment

explanation.definitionFit: A native of Scotland is one national; scot is also an old word for a levy or tax, surviving in 'scot-free'.

clue.text: The certainty of being found guilty

definitions.meaning: the verdict of a court that someone committed a crime

explanation.surface: Someone is sure they will be convicted.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm belief is one sense; a court's guilty verdict is the other.

clue.text: Beneath that boom, English soldiers are concealed

indicators.note: the letters for English soldiers are hidden away inside the word for boom

parts.note: a boom is a loud rumble like thunder
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British army soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops hide under a barrier boom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boom' looks like a harbour barrier, but it is the noise. 'are concealed' puts E and RE inside THUNDER after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal legal adverb meaning under that thing or under those terms.

clue.text: Wipe pan — it is stainless

parts.note: to wipe something is to clean it
to pan a play is to slate it, criticise it harshly

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice: wipe the pan, it's stainless steel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pan' looks like a cooking pot, but it is the verb for savaging a review, which British critics also call to slate.
explanation.definitionFit: A record with no blemishes or past offences is described by this idiom, a fresh start with nothing marked against you.

clue.text: Joint of pork needs some of the stuffing

indicators.note: only part of the words 'pork needs' is used, the letters stuffed inside them

explanation.surface: A cook notes that a joint of pork needs a bit of stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like a joint of meat, but it is the joint in your leg; the run sits across 'pork needs'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinge between thigh and shin is a body joint.

clue.text: Respect nothing that is original in this publication

indicators.note: the letters are given an original, new arrangement

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A periodical prides itself on being original and respecting nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' rearranges RESPECT, O and THAT. The answer is a long-running British weekly political magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A British weekly magazine of politics and culture is a periodical.

clue.text: Take risks in spirited entertainment

definitions.meaning: read literally, a fiery piece of theatre: a stage show featuring flames

explanation.surface: Putting on a lively show can be a risky business.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means courting danger; read word by word it is also a stage drama with flames in it, a fiery show.

clue.text: A koala could be in difficulties

explanation.surface: A koala might be in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in trouble; literally a koala sits high in a eucalyptus.

clue.text: Virginia was one goddess dressed in grey

indicators.note: the goddess is clothed, wrapped inside the colour

parts.note: slate is a blue-grey colour
Vesta is the Roman goddess of the hearth

explanation.surface: Virginia was once a goddess who wore grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virginia' looks like a woman's name but is the US state. 'dressed in' puts VESTA inside SLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Before the American Civil War, states where owning people was legal included Virginia.

clue.text: Padre worked out holy figures

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A priest calculates some sacred numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges PADRE and HOLY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid shapes with many flat faces are geometric figures.

clue.text: Talk Polish inside, getting translated

indicators.note: the polishing word goes in, within the jumbled letters
translating changes the letters of 'side' into a new form

parts.note: to polish hard is to scour

explanation.surface: A conversation in Polish being translated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the language but is the verb. 'inside' splits as 'in' plus SIDE, and 'translated' turns SIDE into DISE, around SCOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal spoken or written treatment of a subject is a talk or lecture.

clue.text: It can stuff

parts.note: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Something that can be used for stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' in the sense of sex appeal (SA) is a standard crossword convention; 'stuff' is a noun meaning fabric, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for cloth or fabric, and this glossy silk weave is one such material.

clue.text: Supplied with information about a number

definitions.meaning: in maths, the phrase introduces known facts about a quantity, as in 'if x equals three'

explanation.surface: Someone was told what a certain figure was.
explanation.definitionFit: Something provided has been handed over; in a maths problem the word introduces a known fact, granting information about a quantity.

clue.text: Docker's about to eat out with surgeons

indicators.note: the letters of the two synonyms are moved about into a new order

parts.note: to eat out or wear away is to erode
vets are animal surgeons

explanation.surface: A dock worker is about to go out for a meal with some doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: An old-style indirect anagram: 'about' shuffles ERODE and VETS together, synonyms not printed in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A labourer who loads and unloads ships is a dock worker.

clue.text: Scholar shortly to become a mother

definitions.text: Scholar shortly to become a mother

parts.words: Scholar shortly to become a mother
parts.note: a degree holder's title, when abbreviated, gives two letters that are also an informal word for mum

explanation.surface: A student will soon be having a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: The degree is abbreviated MA, which is also a word for mother, so 'shortly' this scholar becomes a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A university graduate with this degree is a scholar, and its abbreviation MA is also a childish word for mother.

clue.text: Let in and on

parts.note: the clue joins two phrasal verbs sharing 'let': allow entry, and confess

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to allow someone entry and to confess, 'let on'.

clue.text: City is in Pennsylvania

indicators.note: the word 'is' is placed in the state's abbreviation

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: A city located in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian town famous for its leaning tower is a city.

clue.text: Carp providing food

definitions.meaning: to carp is to complain, to have a grievance

explanation.surface: A fish served up as a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance or grumble is slang 'beef', and the meat of cattle is food.

clue.text: The way to get a gun outside

indicators.note: the word for gun goes outside the letter A, enclosing it

parts.note: rod is old American slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: Instructions for getting a weapon from outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A highway or route is a way to travel.

clue.text: Usually actor's left on time, with swagger

parts.note: punctual means prompt
side is pretentious airs or swagger, as in 'putting on side'

explanation.surface: An actor usually leaves on time, strutting out with a swagger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb (departed) but is the direction: in British theatre the side where the prompter sits is usually stage left, the actor's left.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre, the wing where the prompter stands is normally the performer's left as they face the audience.

clue.text: Need a change? The perfect spot

indicators.note: giving the letters of 'Need' a change rearranges them

explanation.surface: Fancy a holiday? Here's an ideal place to go.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden of the first humans in Genesis is the byword for paradise, an ideal place.

clue.text: Old woman improved by 50%

parts.note: something improved is better
fifty per cent is a half

explanation.surface: A grandmother's health has got half as good again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' is informal slang for one's wife, not an elderly lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are jocular terms for a man's wife or partner.
